claims.text: Equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni can be prepared as a single-phase FCC alloy.
Reducing the number of principal elements from Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni to quaternary or ternary subsets decreases grain-boundary nanocluster formation.
Reducing the number of principal elements dampens local chemical fluctuations near stacking faults.
Separate Cr-, Ni-, and Mn-rich nanoclusters occur at grain boundaries in single-phase CrMnFeCoNi.
Separate Cr-, Ni-, and Mn-rich grain-boundary nanoclusters reduce grain-boundary cohesion.
Reducing grain-boundary nanoclustering should enhance grain-boundary cohesion.
The local chemical environment near a stacking fault strongly affects intrinsic stacking-fault energy in CrCoNi and CrMnFeCoNi.
Local-composition-dependent intrinsic stacking-fault energies span more than 150 mJ/m2 in both CrCoNi and CrMnFeCoNi.
Stacking-fault energy helps govern deformation mechanisms and mechanical performance in these FCC medium- and high-entropy alloys.
A reduced number of elements limits the chemical driving force for formation of separate grain-boundary nanoclusters.
More uniform stacking-fault energies promote more homogeneous deformation and steadier strain hardening.
Grain-boundary decohesion caused by nanoclustering promotes grain-boundary crack initiation in CrMnFeCoNi.
Intermediate-temperature ductility loss in CrMnFeCoNi is correlated with grain-boundary cracking.
Quaternary and ternary subsets will have lower grain-boundary nanocluster incidence than equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi under identical processing.
Quaternary and ternary subsets will have smaller local stacking-fault-energy variations than equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi.
Quaternary and ternary subsets will exhibit delayed grain-boundary cracking and improved uniform ductility relative to equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi.
The proposed mechanism applies broadly to single-phase FCC HEA or MEA systems under similar processing and intermediate-temperature testing regimes.
